claim: EL and EH are two realizations of the same narrow-band, band-limited squared-envelope target under the conditions of section 2.2
scope in which it holds: six acquisitions; β = 0.80, f_s/f_0 = 8–286; cutoff at band centre; largest pixel difference 1.17% of the EH peak
what is not claimed: an exact identity for arbitrary signals, or validity as β approaches 1 or as f_s approaches 2 f_0

claim: Retaining the square narrows the apparent profile by 8–63% relative to envelope stacking and lowers the PSLR in 5/6
scope in which it holds: six in-house phantoms, profile through the target centre
what is not claimed: a resolution gain, or a narrower response in the imaging sense

claim: On the two-point criterion the width ordering does not carry over: at 4:1, M meets the 5% valley criterion at 1.00 mm and EL and EH at 1.50 mm, although EL and EH have the narrower profile
scope in which it holds: one simulated geometry, six realisations, separations 0.40–2.00 mm, amplitude ratios 1:1, 2:1 and 4:1 only, dip criteria of 5% and 20%; C met the criterion at the first separation tested, 0.40 mm
what is not claimed: a continuous resolution limit, C's limiting separation (not measured), a quantitative resolution difference between 0.40 and 0.50 mm, or that the reversal persists at ratios between 2:1 and 4:1, which were not sampled

claim: On gCNR, EL exceeds C in 5/6 datasets and shows no resolved separability advantage over M in any testable dataset
scope in which it holds: six in-house bright-target datasets; EL − C positive in 5/6, W5 saturating and disclosed in section 6; EL − M testable in three datasets and negative in all three, the other three saturating; the sign of EL − M is unchanged under g_m^2, g_m and no geometric compensation
what is not claimed: a general superiority over coherent back-projection, inter-channel phase error as the dominant cause of the EL − C gap (not measured), or equivalence to M, which would require a pre-specified margin

claim: At the common empirical 5% false-alarm design target C needs 2.4 times less amplitude than any incoherent chain (ratio interval 1.96 to 3.12)
scope in which it holds: one simulated geometry, 128-element semicircle; 40 dark draws for the threshold and 20 detection trials per amplitude; 5% is a design target, and the ratio interval resamples the detection trials only
what is not claimed: a certified false-alarm rate, an interval that includes threshold-estimation error, or an operating point transferable to another array, bandwidth or noise model

claim: End-to-end cost does not resolve EL from M; the detection stage is 2.25 times cheaper but 1.3% of the total
scope in which it holds: one machine, ten measured passes after three warm-up passes
what is not claimed: a portable benchmark, or a cost ranking between EL and C that is due to squaring

claim: The per-channel operator is classical; the contribution is its placement between channel and sum
scope in which it holds: a targeted search of Crossref metadata and scholarly web records to 18 October 2026, coded yes only where the record states the operation
what is not claimed: priority, exhaustiveness, or the absence of unpublished and non-indexed precedents
